standard_prerequisites.name: The snake lemma
standard_prerequisites.use: Supplies the connecting map and the exactness of the associated six-term sequence, applied twice inside the proof to extract the two surjectivity statements.

core_obligations: Part (1), preparation (proof lines 1416-1421): replacing the target of the left column by the image of the first horizontal map and the source of the right column by the image of the second horizontal map reduces the situation to one where the first horizontal map of the second row is injective and the second horizontal map of the first row is surjective.

Part (1), first application of the snake lemma (proof lines 1422-1430): the snake lemma applied to the square formed by the last two columns and the kernels of the two right-hand horizontal maps shows that the induced map between those kernels is surjective.

Part (1), second application of the snake lemma (proof lines 1431-1438): the snake lemma applied to the square whose third column is now that kernel gives the surjectivity of the map between the second entries, which is the assertion.
Part (2) (proof lines 1439-1440): the injectivity statement is dual to the surjectivity statement.
proof_roadmap: Reduce by replacing two objects with images so that two of the maps are injective and surjective respectively.
Apply the snake lemma to the kernel square of the right-hand pair of maps.
Apply the snake lemma again with the resulting kernel as the third column.
difficulty_reason: The four lemma gives two surjectivity and injectivity conclusions for a commutative diagram with exact rows (statement lines 1396-1413). The proof is a complete argument for the first assertion: two preparatory replacements reduce to a situation with a convenient injectivity and surjectivity (proof lines 1416-1421), the snake lemma applied to the kernel square of the right-hand pair of maps gives the surjectivity of the induced map between kernels (proof lines 1422-1430), and a second application of the snake lemma, now using that kernel as the third column, gives the surjectivity of the map between the second entries (proof lines 1431-1438); the second assertion follows by duality. The non-formal content is the choice of the two diagrams to which the snake lemma is applied. The claim is H2: a structured argument with each input named.
